method: Direct view_image inspection of the saved native output, against the unchanged prospective testcase.

gates.evidence: Active documentation, a marked crate closure, scale and a clerk holding the trolley defeat a generic warehouse-handling reading. The specifically severed closure state remains ambiguous, so the full prospective conjunction is incomplete.
The primary face is large enough to assess; dark bob, wispy fringe and facial appearance correspond to the portrait. This is appearance correspondence only.

A continuous right forearm leads to the camera grip; camera and subject attention point down toward the marked crate closure. This supports intended documentation, not successful recording or exact optical coverage.
The left gloved hand owns the horizontal scale placed against the crate face below the closure; the closure area is not hidden. No calibrated measurement result is inferred.
Red seal portions appear on both sides of the hasp, but two clearly severed ends separated by an open gap cannot be established at the metal crossing.
A distinct receiving clerk stands behind the crate with both gloved hands wrapped over the trolley handle.
Part of the trolley is visible, but crate-to-platform contact, complete wheels and both actors' feet are cropped or hidden. Plausible support is not complete observable support.
Face, camera, scale and clerk contacts are readable together; decisive seal-gap and support endpoints remain incomplete.
